guard_inventory.rule: Root bytes precede all row checks.
Never infer scope from successful captures.
LICENSE and detected sidecars alone do not prove coverage.
Two TFMs share exact direct/transitive versions; one entry covers multiple obligations; every part of a multipart obligation binds, including 16384-byte text.
Empty complete dependency and asset inventories establish scoped non-applicability.
Nonempty inventories need admitted retained whole-subject no-obligation reviews, not required=false.
One explicitly admitted aggregate represents multiple subjects and parts at exact byte offsets.
A complete reviewed intended location is absent in exact root inspection; other obligations are resolved.
A mapped full entry is a strict nonempty prefix of the required retained bytes, not an arbitrary modified text.
An asset capture does not substitute for the resolved dependency inventory.
Only the admitted graph node count differs; all bytes/reviews/mappings otherwise bind.
Capture diagnostics prevent a complete-closure conclusion.
A dependency capture does not substitute for the bundled-asset inventory.
A passive root LICENSE entry alone is omitted; third-party assets and their mappings remain present.
An unresolved all-entry classification cannot be silently assumed first-party.
Root notice presence does not supply an unavailable dependency archive.
An inventoried bundled asset requires separately checked exact bytes, even when present in the root.
Complete inventories and SPDX metadata alone are insufficient without applicability/obligation reviews.
Unresolved dependency applicability and an unsupported generated-bundle review form use the same conservative review gate; all retained parts and mappings are intact.
Obligation evidence cannot substitute for packaged notice coverage.
One required part lacks a mapping, not a proven missing representation.
All documents agree on the wrong root version; only observed archive identity refutes them.
All document root digests agree with one another, not exact root bytes.
Only the packet assessment digest is wrong.
Only the packet dependency-document digest differs; admission and loader bindings remain correct.
Retained asset bytes and inventory subject digest agree with each other, not the actual root entry.
Only the review's exact subject digest is wrong.
Mapping digest and retained entry agree with each other, not the packaged notice entry.
An extra complete=true assertion is never an admission protocol.
Duplicate identical protocol fields must not be last-wins.
A parent traversal packaged mapping path is rejected before entry lookup.
16385-byte reference text is outside the inclusive 16384-byte profile.
A caller-authored admission producer is unsupported even with matching hashes.
All dependency facts name the wrong version but the archive identity does not.
Arbitrary modified text is not exact coverage and is not automatically a legally incomplete grant.
Retained partial documents and matching hashes do not override the admitted acquisition-unavailable state.
Even byte-identical duplicate archive entries are ambiguous.
Case-equivalent archive entries are not selected by runtime-dependent lookup.
Only the distinct version unique to TFM two has unresolved applicability.
An admitted retained private-contract fact, not failed public acquisition, preempts another complete missing-notice counterexample.
One absent mapping preempts another fully observed missing representation.
A first-node missing archive cannot hide a later-node review digest conflict.
Exact aggregate substrings without explicit aggregate acceptance are insufficient.
Shared loader rejects duplicate-role
Shared loader rejects invalid-relative-path
Shared loader rejects missing-file
Shared loader rejects input-digest-mismatch
Shared loader rejects invalid-fields
Exact retained root alone is not notice coverage.
Exact retained root alone is not notice coverage.
Even zero subjects require an explicitly retained review document.
Every packet/admission/inventory root equals the independent scope root.
Admission binds the entire exact assessment, including all-entry asset scope.
The packet binds the checked admission bytes.
All four admitted document digests bind independently of packet digests.
The complete target multiset equals assessed TFMs; assets cover every root entry without a TFM filter.
Duplicate nodes cannot be silently deduplicated.
Duplicate root edges cannot be silently deduplicated.
Duplicate adjacency edges cannot be silently deduplicated.
Both declared and observed total edge counts obey the same 128-edge limit.
Every root and transitive edge resolves to an inventoried exact node.
Every retained graph node is reachable from root direct edges.
One TFM cannot select competing versions of an ID.
Package inventory equals the complete distinct-version graph union.
Duplicate package records cannot be silently deduplicated.
All-entry inventory paths are unique.
Inventory entry digests match actual root entry bytes.
Bundled-asset keys are unique.
A root entry cannot repeat the same component key.
Only third-party entries have subjects and every such entry has subjects.
One component key cannot be attributed to two root entry locations.
Listed bundled assets equal all third-party entry subjects.
Dependency key matches its inspected identity independently of role/digest.
Dependency roles follow sorted distinct-version indices.
Every dependency archive rejects duplicate, aliased or unsafe entry observations.
Checked dependency bytes match the inventoried digest independently of identity.
Bundled subject keys use the asset namespace.
Asset roles follow sorted component indices.
Asset locations match classified root entry subjects.
Separately checked asset bytes bind the actual inventoried subject digest.
Duplicate whole-subject reviews conflict.
Extra/unassessed-version reviews are not ignored.
Every inventoried subject needs a whole-subject review.
Review admission must be captured even for no-obligation conclusions.
Every review, including no-obligations and owner-private, needs retained basis bytes.
Basis, required part and entry references bind checked evidence paths.
Retained basis and required part references bind checked evidence digests.
Digest/path agreement does not authorize role-agnostic evidence lookup.
Owner-private disposition needs the specific genuinely private fact.
Owner-private reviews cannot simultaneously claim resolved obligations.
Private facts cannot be attached to a non-owner disposition.
An admitted owner-private disposition cannot be ignored before a gap.
No-obligations is empty; obligations is nonempty.
Duplicate obligation IDs cannot be silently deduplicated.
Part IDs are unique per obligation.
Every required part needs its separately checked complete bytes.
Duplicate mappings conflict independently of tuple coverage.
Unknown part/obligation mappings cannot be ignored.
Unknown or unassessed-version mapping subjects cannot be ignored.
An omitted mapping document is not a captured empty mapping.
Mapping admission must be captured even for an empty surface.
Accepted aggregate records have unique paths.
All accepted aggregate paths/digests match inspected root entries.
Absence requires null evidence, zero range and actual observed absence.
Non-absent mappings need an explicit checked entry reference.
A claimed represented packaged entry must actually exist.
Selected entry bytes must be separately retained, not inferred from the root.
A full-entry mapping requires zero offset and full retained length.
Aggregate offsets/lengths must select exactly the complete required bytes.
A partial representation is strictly shorter, not an exact/full representation.
Short unrelated text is not a retained prefix and cannot manufacture a gap.
Entry minimum length and the strict-prefix predicate both exclude empty partial text.
Unused checked evidence roles conflict.
Unresolved review evidence precedes an otherwise supported gap.
Normalized documents use schema version one.
Only the canonical notice-coverage-v1 protocol is accepted.
Each admission component uses its accepted observation/review profile.
Assessment cannot select zero TFMs.
Assessment TFMs are unique, even when graphs agree with duplicates.
Bundled inventory always covers all root entries, not a caller-selected subset.
Each normalized document fits the 65536-byte limit.
Root/dependency archive bytes fit the 8 MiB limit.
Separately retained asset bytes fit the 1 MiB limit.
All checked bytes together fit the 64 MiB limit.
The full all-entry inventory fits the 128-entry profile.
